what_it_does: When building advanced chip packages that combine multiple chips on a single substrate, the different materials expand and contract at different rates when heated, causing the package to warp and bow — similar to how a bimetal strip bends when heated. This warpage degrades performance and can cause failures. This paper proposes an automated tool to account for warpage during the earliest stage of chip design, called floorplanning, where engineers decide where to place major functional blocks. A neural network (specifically a type called a transformer, originally designed for language tasks) learns to understand the design's structure and then generates a placement that minimizes both wire lengths and warpage simultaneously. This is described only at a high level in the abstract; experimental detail is not available.
